ended: Lost the East 1st Round 3-4 to PHI

archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (collapsed series lead)
archetype.definition: A top-five team by net rating that won 56 games and led its first-round series after four games, then lost the next three to Philadelphia and went home in Round 1.

report.headline: A deep, efficient 56-win team that let Philadelphia off the hook

recap.finish: 56-26, first in the Atlantic; lost the East 1st Round 3-4 to PHI
recap.body:
Boston was a methodical, possession-hoarding machine. It played at a 94.8 pace, well below the league's 99.4. It led the league in TOV % at 11.2, ranked 4th in 3PA Rate and owned the 3rd-best REB %. That added up to the 2nd-ranked offense (120.8 ORtg) and the 4th-ranked defense (112.7 DRtg). The slow tempo hides how good it was: the Celtics sat 19th in points scored a game but 1st in points allowed, and their 7.7 differential a game ranked 4th. The roster graded out as one of the league's deepest, with an A+ backcourt and A- wings and frontcourt.

The season started flat and kept climbing. A 3-3 October and an 8-6 November left them 11-9. December (9-3) was the turn, and February was the high point: a 9-2 month with just 98 points allowed a game. They closed 11-5 in March and 6-1 in April and finished 8-2 over their last 10. The longest winning streak was only five games and the longest skid three, so this was a team that rarely lost two in a row rather than one that went on runs. If anything the record undersold it: the margin implied 59 wins, and W vs Pt Diff sat at -3, 24th in the league.

Jaylen Brown carried the scoring with 2,038 points on a 36.2 USG % and 57.3 TS %, and made All-NBA Second Team. Most of the winning, though, came from elsewhere. Neemias Queta led the team in Win Shares (9.0) on a 67.4 TS % with a +9.8 On-Off, and ranks 7th among centers on the site. Derrick White made All-Defensive First Team and posted a +9.7 On-Off despite a 52.9 TS %. Payton Pritchard added 8.5 Win Shares. Brown's -4.6 On-Off says the team held up fine when its top scorer sat. The front line of Queta, Vučević, Garza, Hauser and Walsh is what lifted the rebounding: ORB % rose to 29.2 from 25.7 a year earlier.

The playoffs started like a coronation. Boston won Game 1 by 123-91, split at home, then won both games in Philadelphia, including a 128-96 rout in Game 4. Then the offense dried up. They scored 97, 93 and 100 in the final three games and lost every one, including Games 5 and 7 at home. Boston outscored the 76ers over the series and posted a +3 net rating, 4th among playoff teams, but the two blowouts padded that number. In the close games that decided the series, the shooting failed. Its 52.5% 3PA Rate led the field, but it made just 33.7% of those threes, and its 22.8 FT Rate ranked last of 16. White's TS % fell to 45.0 with a -34.8 On-Off, Brown's On-Off was -31.4, and Vučević shot a 47.7 TS %. Jayson Tatum, who has no regular-season line on the sheet, was the series' best Celtic: 140 points in six games, a 60.8 TS % and an 8.9 BPM.

In context, this is the second straight year a strong regular season led nowhere: six playoff wins in 2024-25 and three this spring, after the 16-win title run of 2023-24. The ratings show a team still near the top, with a 120.8 ORtg against 120.6 last year. What did not change is the structural gap that bit hardest in May: a team that never gets to the line and does not force turnovers has little to fall back on when the threes stop falling.

highlights.title: Elite efficiency at a crawl
highlights.body: Boston ranked 2nd in ORtg and 4th in DRtg while playing far slower than the league, protecting the ball better than anyone. That profile matches 2022-23 through 2024-25, when the offense also ranked 1st or 2nd, so it is a durable identity rather than a fluke.

highlights.title: Queta anchored the frontcourt
highlights.body: Queta led the roster in Win Shares and On-Off on a 67.4 TS %. He drove a rebounding jump to the league's 3rd-best REB %, the best of Boston's recent seasons. He did it on modest usage, so the production doesn't depend on touches.

highlights.title: Better than its record
highlights.body: The point differential implied 59 wins against the 56 Boston actually won. That -3 W vs Pt Diff points to close-game misfortune, not a weak team. The margin also grew as the season went on, peaking at 98 points allowed a game in February.

lowlights.title: Three straight losses to end it
lowlights.body: After winning Game 4 by 32 in Philadelphia, Boston failed to reach 101 points in any of the last three games and lost Games 5 and 7 at home. The series differential was positive, which says the losses came down to cold shooting in tighter games, not being outclassed.

lowlights.title: No free throws, no turnovers forced
lowlights.body: Boston ranked 30th in FT Rate and 27th in Opp TOV %, so it had no cheap points when jumpers stopped falling. That got worse in the playoffs: last of 16 in FT Rate on a field-leading 3PA Rate with 33.7% shooting from three. History shows the same pattern every year.

lowlights.title: Starters went cold in May
lowlights.body: White's TS % sank to 45.0 in the series with a -34.8 On-Off, and Brown's On-Off was -31.4. Vučević managed a 47.7 TS %. White's 52.9 regular-season TS % had already flagged him as the shakiest shooter among the core.

arc.note: From 11-9 after November, Boston won steadily every month, peaked defensively in February and closed 8-2. It then won three of the first four playoff games before losing the last three.

recap.nextYear: The foundation is sound: a top-two offense for a fourth straight year, a top-five defense, an A+ backcourt and A- grades elsewhere. The 56 wins understated a 59-win margin. Brown carried the scoring load, but the efficiency came from Queta, Pritchard and White, so the team does not hinge on one creator. Tatum's playoff line, an 8.9 BPM and 60.8 TS % in six games, shows the top end the regular-season numbers never included. What needs work is the shape of the offense rather than its quality. Last in FT Rate and near the bottom in forcing turnovers, Boston lives on threes, and two springs in a row that has ended early. The close-game luck should even out. The lack of a fallback when shots miss will not fix itself.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season plus a seven-game series; playoff splits are a small sample.
